chunks: Narrated to us the illustrious Sheikh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi, may Allah be pleased with him — he said: my father, may Allah be pleased with him, said: narrated to us Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari — he said: narrated to me Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub — he said: Abd Allah ibn Ghalib al-Asadi informed us, from his father, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn, upon them both be peace, used to admonish the people and make them renounce this world and encourage them in the deeds of

the Hereafter with this speech, every Friday, in the Mosque of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and his family. And it was preserved and written down. He would say: O people! Fear Allah, and know that you will return to Him; then every soul will find what it has done in this world, of good

present, and what evil it has done, it will wish that there were a vast distance between itself and it. And Allah warns you of Himself. Woe to you, O son of Adam — the heedless one, though he is not neglected! O son of Adam, verily your appointed time is the fastest thing approaching you; it has already come towards you swiftly, seeking you, and is about to catch up with you. And it is as if you have already fulfilled your term, and the angel has seized your soul, and you have gone to your grave alone. Then your soul is returned to you, and your two angels, Munkar and Nakir, enter upon you forcefully for your questioning and rigorous testing. Know that the first thing they will ask you about is your Lord whom you used to worship, and about your Prophet who was sent to you, and about your religion which you used to practice, and about your Book which you used to recite, and about your Imam whom you used to follow. Then about your life — how you spent it — and your wealth, from where you acquired it and on what you spent it. So take your precautions, look after your soul, and prepare your answer before the examination, the questioning, and the trial. For if you are a believing, God-fearing person, knowledgeable of your religion, a follower of the truthful ones, and devoted to the guardians of Allah,

Allah will inspire your proof and make your tongue speak with the right answer, and you will answer well and be given glad tidings of Paradise and the pleasure and most beautiful blessings of Allah, and the angels will receive you with mercy and sweet fragrance. But if you are not such, your tongue will falter, your argument will be refuted, and you will be unable to give the answer, and you will be given news of the Fire, and the angels of punishment will receive you with a welcoming of boiling water and roasting in the Hellfire. So know, O son of Adam, that beyond this lies something still greater, more horrifying, and more painful for hearts — the Day of Resurrection. That is a Day for which all people will be assembled, and that is a Day that will be witnessed. Allah will gather in it the former and the latter generations. That is a Day when the Trumpet will be blown and the graves will be scattered.

That is the Day of the Impending — when hearts will be at throats, while they are suppressing. That is a Day when no stumble will be excused, no ransom will be taken from anyone, no excuse will be accepted from anyone, and there will be no future opportunity for repentance for anyone. There is nothing
the recompense for good deeds and the recompense for evil deeds. So whoever among the believers has done in this world the weight of an atom of good will find it, and whoever

among the believers has done in this world the weight of an atom of evil will find it. So beware, O people, of disobedience and sins, for indeed Allah has forbidden you from them and warned you against them in the Truthful Book and the clear Speaking explanation. And do not feel safe from the scheming of Allah and the severity of His punishment when the accursed Satan calls you to the fleeting desires and pleasures of this

world. For verily Allah says: Verily those who are God-fearing, when a visitation from Satan touches them, they remember, and behold they see clearly. So imbue your hearts with the fear of Allah and remember what Allah has promised you upon your return to Him of His beautiful reward, just as He has warned you

of severe punishment. For verily whoever fears something is wary of it, and whoever is wary of something avoids it. So do not be of the heedless who incline toward the splendor of the life of this world, for then you would become of those who devise evil schemes. And indeed Allah the Exalted said: Do they feel secure — those who devise evil deeds — that Allah will cause the earth to sink with them, or that the punishment will come to them from

where they do not perceive, or seize them in their going about — for they cannot thwart Him — or seize them with a gradual reduction. For verily your Lord is indeed Most Kind, Most Merciful. So beware of what Allah has warned you, and take heed from what He did with the oppressors in His Book. And do not feel safe that some of what He threatened the oppressive people with in the Book will descend upon you. By Allah, you have indeed been admonished through others, and verily the truly fortunate is the one who takes heed from others. And verily Allah has made you hear in

the Book what He did with the oppressive people from the inhabitants of the towns before you, where He said: And how many oppressive towns We have destroyed, and raised up other peoples after them. And when they sensed Our might,
behold they flee from it. That is, they run away. Do not flee, and return to what you were given in luxury and your dwellings, perhaps you will
will be questioned. But when the punishment came to them, they said: O woe to us — verily we were oppressors! And that remained their cry until We made them
stubble, extinguished. And by Allah, verily this is indeed an admonition and a warning for you, if you take heed and fear. Then he returned to the speech from Allah in the Book against the people of

disobedience and sins, saying: And if ever a breath of the punishment of your Lord touches them, they will certainly say: O woe to us — verily we were oppressors! But if you say, O people, that Allah only meant by this the people of polytheism, then how is that, while He says: And We shall set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, and no soul will be wronged anything — and if it is the weight of a grain of mustard seed, We will bring it forth, and sufficient are We as Reckoners. Know, O servants of Allah, that the people of polytheism — the scales will not be set up for them,
And the registers of deeds will not be spread open for them; they are spread open only for the people of Islam. So fear Allah, O servants of Allah, and know that Allah

He did not choose this world and its immediate pleasures for any of His friends, nor did He make them desirous of it and of its fleeting bloom and outward beauty. Rather, He created the world and created its people to test which of them is best in deed for his Hereafter. By Allah, He has indeed set forth for you examples in it and varied the signs for a people who reason. So be, O believers, among the people who reason. And there is no power except with Allah. Be ascetic in what He has made you ascetic.

Allah in the immediate pleasures of the life of this world. For Allah says — and His word is the truth — 'The likeness of the life of this world is but as water which We send down from the sky, and it mingles with
the vegetation of the earth, of which people and cattle eat, until, when the earth has taken on

its adornment and was adorned, and its inhabitants thought they had power over it — Our command came to it by night or by day, and We made it a harvested field as if it had not flourished yesterday. Thus We explain the signs for a people who reflect. So be, O servants of Allah, among the people who reflect. And do not incline toward the world, for Allah has indeed said to Muhammad, His Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family, and to his companions: 'And do not incline toward those who have wronged, lest the Fire touch you.' And do not incline toward the bloom of the life of this world and what is in it, with the inclination of one who has taken it as a permanent abode and dwelling place.

key_terms.الإمام: The Imam — the fifth question in the grave interrogation, a distinctively Shia doctrine
key_terms.التقوى: God-consciousness, piety — the fundamental spiritual orientation determining righteous action and ultimate salvation
key_terms.الصادقين: The truthful ones — referring in the Shia tradition to the Imams and the Prophet
key_terms.الموازين: The just scales — the scales of justice on the Day of Resurrection
key_terms.مثقال ذرة: The weight of an atom — expressing the precision of divine reckoning
key_terms.منكر ونكير: Munkar and Nakir — the two angels who question the deceased in the grave about their Lord, Prophet, religion, Book, and Imam

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin say about the grave questioning, the Day of Judgment, and detachment from the world?
ai.summary: This is a Friday sermon delivered weekly by Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin (peace be upon them both) in the Mosque of the Prophet during the Umayyad period. The Imam uses the setting of the grave questioning by Munkar and Nakir — with the distinctively Shia element of being asked about one's Imam — to teach accountability before God, the reality of the Hereafter, and the importance of detachment from worldly life. He cites multiple Quranic verses and concludes with a du'a for divine support in piety and asceticism.

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Abdullah b. Ja`far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad narrated to me from al-Hasan b. Mahbub. He said: `Abdullah b. Ghalib al-Asadi informed me from his father from Sa`id b. al-Musayyib. He said: `Ali b.

al-Husayn (as) would exhort the people, encourage them to be ascetic in this world, and make them desirous of deeds for the next world with these words every Friday in the Mosque of the Messenger (s). It was memorized and written down. He would say: O people! Fear Allah and know that you will return to Him. Every soul will find what they did of good in this world and what they did of evil. He will wish there was a far expanse between him and his deeds. Allah warns you of Himself.

Woe to you, O son of Adam, for you are negligent, but not neglected. O son of Adam! Your term is the quickest thing to come to you, and it approaches you vigorously, and it seeks you wanting to catch you. It is as though you have fulfilled your term [already], and the angel has taken your spirit, and you are alone in your grave. Your spirit returns to you, and the two angels Munkar and Nakir ask you and interrogate you severely. The first thing they will ask you about is your Lord that you would worship, your prophet that was sent to you, your religion that you would take to, your Book that you would recite, and your Imam that you would align with! Then, [they will ask about] your time and how you lived it, your wealth and how you gained it and how you spent it. So, be cautious, look into yourself, and recount the answers before you are interrogated and questioned.

If you are a Godfearing believer who is knowledgeable in your religion, obedient to the truthful ones (al-sadiqin), and aligning with the friends of Allah, Allah will accept your proof, and He will cause your tongue to speak the best answers, and you will be given the glad tidings of Paradise, the contentment of Allah, and goodly things. The angels will receive you with comfort and sweetness. If you are not [righteous], then your tongue will stammer, your proof will be rejected, and you will not be able to respond. You will be given tidings of the Fire, and you will be received by the angels of torment. You will descend into boiling water and you will be sent to Hell. So, know, O son of Adam, that the Day of Resurrection is greater, more terrible, and more painful to the hearts. That is the Day that the people will be gathered to; that is a day that is witnessed. Allah will gather the former and the latter people in it. That is the day in which the trumpet will be blown, and the graves will be turned over.

That is the approaching day in which [it is as though] the hearts will be in the throats. That is the day in which no falsehood will be said, no ransom will be taken from anyone, no excuse will be accepted from anyone, and no repentance will be accepted from anyone.

There will be nothing except the recompense for good deeds and the recompense for sins. If a believer does even an atom’s weight of good in this world, he will find it [on the Day of Resurrection]; and if a believer does even an atom’s weight of evil in this world, he will find it.

So, beware, O people, of disobedience and sin, for Allah has prohibited you from that and has warned you of that in the truthful Book and the Speaking Elucidation. Do not feel secure against the plotting of Allah and the intensity of His seizing when the accursed Satan calls to you through desires and pleasures in this world.

Surely, Allah says, “When Satan whispers to the Godfearing, they remember [Him], then they have insight.” [7:201] Legislate your heart upon the fear of Allah and remember what Allah has promised you of His goodly rewards in your return to Him, just as He has frightened you from stern reprisal, for whoever fears a thing becomes careful of it, and whoever is careful of a thing avoids it.

Do not be of the heedless ones, who lean toward the caprice of the life of this world, and who make evil plots. Allah says, “Do those who devise evil plots feel secure that Allah will not cause the earth to swallow them? Or that the torment will not come upon them in ways they cannot comprehend?

Or that He will not seize them while they go about, for then they will have no escape? Or that He will not destroy them gradually? But your Lord is truly Ever Gracious, Most Merciful.” (16:45-47) So, be cautious of what Allah has called you to be cautious of and observe what He did to the oppressors in His Book. Do not consider yourselves secure from that which He promised to bring down against the oppressors in the Book. Allah has admonished you through others – surely, happy is him who is admonished through others.
Allah has made you hear of what He did to the oppressors in the world before you in the Book when He said, “How many societies of wrongdoers We have destroyed, raising up other people after them!
When the wrongdoers sensed Our torment, they started to run away from their cities. ‘Do not run away! Return to your luxuries and your homes, so you may be questioned.’
They cried, ‘Woe to us! We have surely been wrongdoers.’ They kept repeating their cry until We mowed them down, lifeless.”

(21:11-15) I swear by Allah, surely, this is an admonition and an intimidation for you; return to the saying of Allah about the people of disobedience and sin in the Book, “If they were touched by even a breath of your Lord’s torment, they would certainly cry, ‘Woe to us! We have really been wrongdoers.’” [21:46] If you say, O people, that Allah only meant the pagans [here], then how can that be when He says, “We will set up the scales of justice on the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in the least. And if a deed is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as a Reckoner.” [21:47]?

Know, O servants of Allah, that the scales and the records will not be brought out for pagans. The records will only be brought out for the people of Islam. So, fear Allah, O servants of Allah, and know that Allah did not choose this world for any of His friends, nor did He cause them to desire it, its caprice, and its apparent joys. He only created this world and its people to test them [and see] which of them are best in their deeds for their Hereafter. I swear by Allah, Allah has presented similitudes for you, and He presented verses for a people who think.
So be, O believers, of those who think – and there is no power except by Allah.

Be ascetic in that which Allah kept away from you from the life of this world, for Allah says – and His words are truth, “The life of this world is just like rain We send down from the sky, producing a mixture of plants which humans and animals consume.

Then just as the earth looks its best, perfectly beautified, and its people think they have full control over it, there comes to it Our command by night or by day, so We mow it down as if it never flourished yesterday! This is how We make the signs clear for people who reflect.” [10:24] So, be, O servants of Allah, of those who think, and do not incline toward this world, for Allah said to His Prophet Muhammad (s) and his companions, “And do not be inclined to the wrongdoers or you will be touched by the Fire.” [11:113] Do not incline toward the caprice of the life of this world in the way of those who inclined toward it and took it as their decisive abode and settlement house, for it is an evicting abode, an abode that just suffices, and an abode of work. So, increase in your righteous works therein before you leave it and before Allah permits its ruin. The One who will ruin it is the One who built it up the first time and initiated it; and He is the guardian of its bequeathal. I ask Allah to support us and you in increasing our God-consciousness and our asceticism. May Allah make us and you among the ascetic ones in the caprice of the life of this world, and among the desirous workers for the reward of the Hereafter; for we can only act by Him, and we are His.
